title: Belle Gunness, Part 9: The Brother Who Came Looking (LaPorte, 1908)
notes: History only. No bodies or remains shown or described; 'found his brother' is as far as it goes. The 'wild rapture' letter is not used (HistoryNet: not authentic). No money figure (sources differ: $2,839, $1,800) and no length of stay (1 or 2 weeks). Hometown only 'South Dakota' (Aberdeen rests on the museum alone). No claim about the farm site today. Blind fact-check Nov. 21: the house was red brick (drawn brick); more than one farmhand dug ('with farmhands'); 'the first discovery on that farm' was wrong (the fire victims were found first), now 'It was only the beginning.' Second check: 'Days later' (he came in early May); 'the hired man and others' (Maxson plus a few men); 'near LaPorte'; McClung Road confirmed by Indiana Public Media and Crime Library.

sources.what: 'Andrew Helgelien, a Norwegian farmer from Aberdeen, South Dakota'; Andrew 'had money sent from his bank account in Aberdeen to the First National Bank in La Porte'; Asle 'wrote to Belle and the bank asking about Andrew'; Belle said he had left; after the fire 'Asle Helgelien came from South Dakota to La Porte'; 'Joe Maxson and Asle began digging on the farm in an area where Joe and Belle had buried garbage in March'
sources.who: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum, Belle Gunness exhibit

sources.what: letters from Aug. 8, 1906 to Dec. 9, 1907, about 80 found by Asle; Nov. 22, 1906 letter: 'have all the money changed into bills'; a visit in January 1908; Asle 'never believed her replies'; went to LaPorte in early May 1908 after the fire and urged digging beyond the ruins

about 80 letters over roughly 16 months; 'This is a secret between us'; Andrew came in early January 1908 and the money was withdrawn; Asle wrote in March; on May 4 Asle went to the LaPorte sheriff; Asle recognized his brother
'Change all the cash you have into paper bills'; dozens of letters
'A. K. Helgelin, whose inquiries regarding his missing brother led to the first discoveries on the Gunness farm'
Asle didn't believe Belle's claims; he came to LaPorte and found his brother in a pit of household waste
his search for his brother led to a hog pen, where men started digging; reported May 5, 1908

the house: 'a square house of red brick... two stories high' beside McClung Road; the dig in 'a large garbage pit behind the house near the hog pen' by Joe Maxson and Daniel Hutson; Asle: 'That's my brother!'
sources.who: Crime Library, Belle Gunness, chapters 5 and 10

sources.what: the farm on McClung Road near LaPorte
sources.who: Indiana Public Media, Moment of Indiana History

beats.text: Her letters brought him to LaPorte, Indiana. He never came home. His brother came looking.
beats.label: LAPORTE, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum; HistoryNet

beats.text: Andrew Helgelien was a Norwegian farmer in South Dakota. Belle Gunness sent him about 80 letters.
beats.label: SOUTH DAKOTA
beats.credit: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum; HistoryNet; Mental Floss

beats.text: They told him to change his money into bills, and to keep it a secret.
beats.label: HER LETTERS

beats.text: In January 1908, he came to her farm. His money was drawn from a LaPorte bank, and he was gone.
beats.label: JANUARY 1908
beats.credit: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum; HistoryNet; Mental Floss

beats.text: His brother Asle wrote to Belle. She said Andrew had left. Asle didn't believe her.
beats.label: ASLE HELGELIEN
beats.credit: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum; HistoryNet; AP, 2008

beats.text: On April 28, her farmhouse burned. Days later, Asle came to LaPorte and went to the sheriff.
beats.label: APRIL 28, 1908
beats.credit: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum; HistoryNet; Mental Floss

beats.text: He dug with the hired man and others where garbage had been buried. There, Asle found his brother. It was only the beginning.
beats.label: MAY 1908
beats.credit: LaPorte County Historical Society Museum; Crime Library; Astorian, 1908
